Fire TV Cube 3rd gen (gazelle / PS7717) — unlock, Magisk & TWRP

Disclaimer

You do this at your own risk. A bad flash can hard-brick the device and there is no official recovery path. I am not responsible for bricked Cubes, angry spouses or missed football games.

Requirements

  • Fire TV Cube 3rd gen (gazelle), firmware PS7717 0.0.1.3 or lower — check with getprop ro.build.display.id
  • A Linux PC (a live USB works) with python3, pyusb and fastboot
  • USB-A to USB-A cable, or the micro-USB port with an OTG adapter
  • The files attached to this post (payload, patched TWRP, boot.img for your build)

Steps

  1. Block OTA updates first: firetv-ota-block (no root needed).
  2. Unplug power, hold the Action button and plug the USB cable in. The LED ring should stay dark.
  3. Run the exploit and wait for the bootloader to report unlocked:
Code:
sudo ./bootrom-step.sh
# wait for:  [+] Found device, sending payload
sudo python3 amonet.py --unlock
    [+] bootloader: unlocked
    [+] rpmb: patched

4. Flash TWRP and boot into it:
Code:
fastboot flash recovery twrp-3.7.0_gazelle.img
fastboot oem reboot-recovery

5. In TWRP, flash Magisk-v27.0.zip (rename the .apk) and reboot. Done.



2026-10-20 – payload v4, fixes RPMB timeout on 0.0.1.3
2026-09-02 – TWRP 3.7.0, decrypt works
2026-08-14 – initial release

Source and issue tracker: https://github.com/example/gazelle-unlock

GitHub - example/gazelle-unlock: Bootrom exploit, unlock and TWRP for the Fire TV Cube 3rd gen

Bootrom exploit, unlock and TWRP for the Fire TV Cube 3rd gen - example/gazelle-unlock
github.com

Thanks to @amlogic_annie for the RPMB notes and @gazelle_dev for testing.

Q: Does this work on the 2nd gen (raven)?
A: No. Use the raven thread.

sideload_sam said:
Mine lights up blue every time I plug it in, even holding the button. Am I doing something wrong?
Click to expand...
You are plugging power first. Power must be unplugged; the USB cable alone powers the SoC in bootrom mode. Check dmesg, you should see:
Code:
usb 1-2: New USB device found, idVendor=0e8d, idProduct=0003

magiskfan_88 said:
Is there a way to keep Alexa hands-free working after rooting?
Click to expand...
Yes, it's the DSP firmware being disabled by one of the debloat scripts. Re-enable it:
Code:
adb shell
su
pm enable com.amazon.alexa.voice
setprop persist.vendor.dsp.wakeword 1
reboot
More details in my notes, section Wakeword.
 
Amlogic tools & notes: github.com/example/amlogic-notes
